key_insight: In laser-TIG hybrid welding of Invar steel, higher laser power increases penetration and keyhole size but can deflect the arc, while higher travel speed reduces heat input and higher current broadens the weld and stabilizes the arc.
engineering_relevance: The results provide process guidance for tuning hybrid welding parameters to control molten pool flow, weld geometry, and arc stability in low-CTE Invar steel fabrication.
method: Numerical simulation of molten pool fluid dynamics
High-speed photography of arc and pool behavior
Parameter study across laser power, welding speed, and current
evidence_signal: The abstract reports observed trends over laser power of 5–6 kW, welding speed of 0.5–0.8 m/min, and current of 150–170 A, linking each to measurable changes in penetration, weld width, flow, and arc behavior.
watch_item: The findings are parameter-window specific, so direct transfer to other joint setups, thicknesses, or shielding conditions may require re-optimization.
paper_title: Molten pool dynamic behavior and arc characteristics in laser-TIG hybrid welding of Invar steel
